title: Increasing Durability of Dissociated Neural Cell Cultures Using Biologically Active Coralline Matrix
protocol: Break the coral skeleton into fragments measuring 0.5–2 cm using a hammer.
Soak the coral skeleton fragments in a 10% sodium hypochlorite solution for 10 minutes.
Wash the fragments once with double distilled water (DDW).
Submerge the fragments in a 1M NaOH solution for 5 minutes.
Rinse the fragments once with DDW.
Immerse the fragments in a 30% H2O2 solution for 10 minutes.
Rinse the fragments three times with DDW.
Dry the coral fragments in the hood for 1 to 8 hours.
Transfer glass coverslips into a 100 mm glass Petri dish.
Add 10 mL of 95% ethanol to the Petri dish containing the glass coverslips.
Incubate at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Remove ethanol and wash with distilled deionized water (DDW) three times, waiting 10 minutes between each wash.
Place the dish on an 80°C pre-warmed heating plate until all DDW evaporates.
Gently stir the coverslips within the plate several times while drying to prevent them from sticking to each other.
Autoclave the coverslips.
Grind coral skeleton fragments using a mortar and pestle until complete breakdown occurs.
Alternatively, grind coral skeleton fragments using an electrical grinding machine at 1,000 rpm for 30 seconds.
Transfer ground grains onto a manual or electrical 40 µm filter mesh strainer.
Divide the grains into two specific size ranges by sieving through the strainer.
Add coral skeleton grains into a 20 µg/mL poly-D-lysine (PDL) solution dissolved in Hanks' solution.
Pour the PDL-grain solution into flasks and dishes (approximately 2 mL/25 cm²).
Incubate overnight at 4 °C.
Wash the flasks and dishes once with sterile DDW.
Let the flasks and dishes dry in the hood.
Add coral skeleton grains to DDW at any desired concentration.
Pour 40 µL of the grain solution onto the center of the coverslip.
Place the coverslips on a heating plate prewarmed to 80 °C.
Wait for complete evaporation until the grains adhere to the coverslip (usually 15 min).
Autoclave the coated coverslips.
Store the autoclaved coverslips in sterile conditions.
A day before culture, place the coverslips on the lid of a sterile 24 well plate.
Add 100 µL of 20 µg/mL PDL solution to each coverslip.
Ensure that the liquid covers the entire grain region and the rest of the coverslip surface using the tip.
Cover the lid with the bottom of the plate.
Wrap the sides of the plates with paraffin film.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C.
The next day, wash once with distilled deionized water (DDW).
Dry the coverslips in the hood.
Prepare an empty 60 mm Petri dish.
Pour 2 mL of minimal essential medium (MEM) into a 60 mm Petri dish and put on ice.
Pour 2 mL of MEM into a 35 mm dish and put it in an incubator at 37 °C, 5–10% CO2.
Pour 2 mL of MEM into a 15 mL tube and keep it at 4 °C.
Pour 1 mL of First Day Medium into a 15 mL tube and put it in an incubator at 37 °C, 5-10% CO2.
Thaw 200 µL of a 2.5% trypsin solution and incubate at 37 °C.
Prepare three glass Pasteur pipettes with 0.5 mm, 0.75 mm, and 1.0 mm diameter heads using a flame.
Prepare adequate surgical tools: one big scissor, two small scissors, one big tweezer, four small tweezers, and one scalpel.
Prepare a stereomicroscope in the hood.
Sacrifice 0–3 day old Sprague Dawley rat pups by separating their heads from their bodies into an empty 60 mm Petri dish with a big scissor.
Dispose of the bodies.
Pick up the head by holding it from the mouth with a big tweezer.
Cut the skin covering the skull with a small scissor.
Enter beneath the skull (on the side of the cerebellum) and cut the skull to the right and to the left to enable its removal with a clean scissor.
Peel the skull off from the brain using a clean tweezer.
Separate the brain from the head and put it in a 60 mm Petri dish containing 2 mL of cold MEM.
Dissect the hippocampi under a stereomicroscope using two small tweezers.
Transfer the hippocampi into the prepared 35 mm dish containing MEM.
Cut the hippocampi to approximately 1 mm slices using the scalpel.
Add 200 µL of the trypsin solution diluted to a final concentration of 0.25%.
Mix gently and incubate at 37 °C, 5–10% CO2 for 30 min.
Add 2 mL of cold MEM to the dish to deactivate trypsin.
Transfer the trypsinized tissue to a 15 mL tube containing 1 mL First Day Medium preheated to 37 °C using the largest diameter glass Pasteur pipette.
Triturate the tissue by passing it through the largest diameter glass pipette 10–15 times.
Repeat trituration with the medium diameter glass pipette.
Continue triturating with the smallest diameter pipette.
Let remaining tissue pieces sink for 2–5 min, then transfer the supernatant into another 15 mL tube.
Count cells using a hemocytometer.
Dilute or concentrate cells to achieve a density of 200,000–400,000 cells/mL using First Day Medium.
Seed 100 µL of cells on each glass coverslip ensuring complete coverage.
Incubate at 37 °C in an atmosphere of 5–10% CO2.
Add 500 µL of Neuronal Growth Medium to the wells the next day.
Transfer each coverslip to its appropriate well using a tweezer while tilting the coverslip to remove the First Day Medium.
Suction the remaining media from the lid.
Incubate at 37 °C, 5–10% CO2.
Maintain cultures under these conditions up to 1 month.
Ensure the incubator is maximally humidified.
